name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: US tariffs reset under Section 301; new Russia-linked tariff powers signed
state: After the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb, the US moved to 10–12.5% Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies from 24 Jul; the average effective rate was 7.1% in August (Yale Budget Lab). China's pause on some rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov with no renewal announced, a possible new flashpoint.
for_you: Tariffs are lower than in 2025 but policy remains unpredictable, and new threats could quickly change trade costs.
rubric_hit: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.

sources.title: Penn Wharton Budget Model — Effective tariff rates, updated 14 Oct
Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
